subject: Both live tournaments still use the LEGACY PUBLIC joinCode fallback, so the join gate is no gate
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-19 against production, read-only. TOURN-03 built the correct architecture: the authoritative code lives at tournaments/{id}/private/config (rules deny it to every client, verified live: unauthenticated GET = 403) and hasJoinCode is the public boolean. The console writes that on CREATE (console.html:11211). But NO MIGRATION was ever written for tournaments created before the fix, and BOTH live tournaments are pre-fix: private/config exists=false, hasJoinCode=false, PUBLIC joinCode field present (7 chars) on a doc that is allow read:if true. ctfJoinTeam therefore takes its documented legacy fallback (functions/index.js:7969). Consequence: an anonymous stranger reads the code with one unauthenticated REST GET and joins Special Event, which is ACTIVE. This is the exact defect TOURN-03 proved and closed for NEW events only. CRITICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR THE OPERATOR'S PLANNED ACTION: rotating the join code does NOT fix this - a new code written to the same public field is equally published. Rotation and migration must be the SAME operation. Remedy is the flagSecrets pattern already shipped: two-phase COPY (write private/config + hasJoinCode, leave the public field so the running event does not break) then PURGE (remove the public field once the private copy is confirmed).
[2026-09-20 02:07] WORDING CORRECTION (Chris, 2026-09-19): this item's description says private/config is denied 'to every client'. That is imprecise and I repeated it several times. firestore.rules:1491 allows isAdmin() explicitly - the comment there even says ADMIN-ONLY, not nobody. The property that actually matters, and that is directly tested and passes, is that a signed-in NON-ADMIN cannot read it. Read every 'denied to every client' in this item as 'denied to every non-admin client'. The security claim is unaffected; the wording was wrong.
